No theorem gives L(N) = omega(log N) infinitely often; the longest known prime APs in [1,N] have length far below log N and the o(log N) question is open. 'negative close achieved' is a citation misuse.

Gaussian prime 3 has no Gaussian prime at unit distance (2,4,3±i all composite), so L1 fails; repair requires step bound √2, which still leaves the canonical infinite-path/moat question open in both branches.
